evals.prompt: Setup agent evaluation for this project using Halios.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the agent, installs the Halios CLI if missing, uses separate auth/project setup, writes the three-file executable skeleton plus optional local discovery notes for unresolved work, configures stock OTel plus a jsonl-v1 adapter, authors supportable evals/scenarios, and runs exactly one fresh k=1 smoke scenario when safe prerequisites exist. It summarizes verified evidence, pending/unverified work and next inputs, includes available CLI-provided review links, and stops without running the full bank or editing agent behavior. It does not invent a smoke case or claim completion when required evidence is unavailable.

evals.prompt: This production trace failed. Turn it into a regression and fix the agent: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
evals.expected_output: Retrieves stable JSON evidence and the CLI-provided trace link, generates a scenario from intent rather than replaying assistant output, makes one focused code change, reruns the failure plus protected scenarios once, then summarizes with exact run/trace review links and stops instead of entering another repair cycle.

evals.prompt: Our eval suite is passing. Try prompt optimization but don't weaken the safety checks.
evals.expected_output: Verifies suite health, freezes an immutable baseline, uses backend guidance for one bounded coding-agent prompt edit at a time, records unchanged-suite evidence, applies only a backend-accepted candidate, verifies protected gates, and provides the CLI-returned optimization and final evaluation links for review.

evals.prompt: Our Python agent already exports OpenTelemetry spans. Halios shows the tool names, but every tool says no arguments or result captured. Fix the instrumentation without replacing our tracer provider.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the emitted semantic attributes and existing tracer setup, preserves the existing provider, uses current structured OTel GenAI tool arguments/results, verifies normalized tool kind/input/output with halios trace verify on a fresh runtime trace, and does not put telemetry logic in only the eval adapter.

evals.prompt: Connect this multi-agent RAG service to Halios. It uses a router agent, two specialist sub-agents, a vector database, a reranker, and several tools, with some OpenTelemetry already installed.
evals.expected_output: Inventories existing instrumentation, models a single W3C trace with nested agent, model, tool, retrieval, and reranker spans, captures the minimum structured evidence and identities, applies privacy controls, and verifies both production-runtime and eval-adapter traces before running evaluations.

evals.prompt: Add a GitHub Actions release gate for this agent and instrument our staging deployment. Be clear about whether the Halios adapter runs in staging.
evals.expected_output: Adapts the bundled CI workflow, uses API and agent-scoped OTLP secrets without persisting credentials, runs adapter-based simulation only in the evaluation job, instruments the real staging runtime directly with deployment.environment.name=staging and immutable service.version, and verifies a real staging smoke trace after deployment.

evals.prompt: Tell me what's failing in prod for this Halios agent and turn the biggest recurring failure into a regression.
evals.expected_output: Uses production trace list, failed evaluator evidence, and clustering queries; distinguishes missing telemetry or missing check execution from no failures; verifies a representative trace; then drafts a sanitized regression from intent and preserves stable evidence IDs.

evals.prompt: Why is the release blocked? The GitHub Halios check is red.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the GitHub run and immutable Halios run report, identifies whether setup, adapter, telemetry, check execution, protected behavior, threshold, or trusted publication caused the block, cites the relevant IDs and fields, and recommends a focused fix rather than a blind rerun.

evals.prompt: Set up Halios evals for this customer-support agent. Configure everything and prove the integration works, but I have not decided how large the full evaluation should be.
evals.expected_output: Completes setup and exactly one k=1 smoke scenario, reports verification evidence with a compact Review in Halios section using CLI-returned suite/run/trace links, and stops. It does not infer a full-suite trial count, run the bank, inspect behavioral failures beyond the smoke summary, or modify the prompt/code. It asks whether to run the full suite and how many trials per scenario to use.

evals.prompt: The Halios suite is already configured. Run the full evaluation with four trials per scenario and tell me what failed.
evals.expected_output: Runs halios eval run -k 4 exactly once, retrieves and reports failure evidence with the CLI-provided exact run and representative trace links, and stops without modifying the agent or rerunning. It does not substitute the default k=3 or begin a repair loop.

evals.prompt: Diagnose why this Halios run failed and recommend what we should change: run_123.
evals.expected_output: Retrieves the run, scenario, and trace/check evidence; explains the likely cause and recommends a focused change; includes the CLI-provided exact run and trace links for visual review; and stops without editing files or starting another evaluation.

evals.prompt: The Halios setup smoke test finished. Give me a concise handoff so I can review what was created without having to search around the dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Provides a short Review in Halios section with no more than five CLI-provided links: agent overview, scenarios, rules/rubrics, exact smoke run, and representative trace. It briefly says what can be verified in the UI, does not invent routes or expose credentials, and does not make opening the UI mandatory.

evals.prompt: Design Halios evals locally for our document assistant. Its prompt says: answer user questions using search_documents(query: string), cite the returned document IDs, and never invent facts. The tool accepts a nonempty query and returns [{id, text}]. The source is a private remote service; no corpus, metadata, trace samples, or typical user questions are available in this checkout. Author what you can and tell me what remains. Do not connect, install, run the application, or run evaluations.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes retrieval-backed behavior despite the generic prompt; creates only supportable draft checks/cases in the existing suite; records unresolved knowledge discovery in discovery.yml with stable IDs, affected coverage and an actionable next step; asks for seed questions, source samples, or existing access details without secrets; does not invent source truth, a second suite, full recall, or successful runtime verification.

evals.prompt: Our refund workflow has no document search. Code exposes issue_refund(order_id, amount). Policy says ask for an order ID and obtain approval for high-value refunds, but nobody has specified the amount threshold. Draft the supportable Halios checks/scenarios locally. Do not call the real refund tool, configure a server suite, or run evaluations. Explain what you completed and what you still need.
evals.expected_output: Continues with the known order-ID/tool requirements, records the missing approval threshold as a non-RAG discovery gap, asks a targeted policy question, and does not guess an amount or make a real refund. Reports drafts versus unconfigured/unverified work and keeps expected answers out of simulator context.

evals.prompt: Read-only review: our configured Halios smoke run passed. Existing discovery notes still say production trace verification is pending and the domain corpus is inaccessible. Are we fully covered? Do not edit files, run anything, or deploy.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the passed smoke covers the configured suite only, retains both unresolved limitations, recommends specific next inputs/actions, and does not edit the notes, mark gaps resolved, run/deploy, or claim complete coverage. Proposes any discovery updates in the response only.
